title: Gate listener session pairing on operator approval
description:
HTTP integration prerequisite for P1.1. Consume the pairing-approval window from task-959df79da24442eeb84d446284ff3357 and replace token redemption with three bounded same-origin routes: request a pending pairing, claim only an approved request, and approve a confirmation label only after the existing HTTP authenticator admits a project.admin principal.

DELIVERABLE: listener guards and route handlers with exact request shapes, auth/capability ordering, stable refusal code/layer, one approved request minting one real operator session through the existing SessionHandshakePort, and no response/log/request-line disclosure of any credential.

NOT IN SCOPE: daemon token emission cleanup, launcher stdin/browser opening, control-room UI, or changing session capability/TTL semantics.

SAFETY ORDERING: the state-machine task must be delivered first. Until daemon/launcher/browser consumers migrate, old clients fail closed; no legacy token redemption fallback is allowed.

VERIFICATION COMMAND: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon exec vitest run --root . --config package.json src/http/http-listener-handshake.test.ts`; it must exit 0 with nonzero Test Files and Tests counts.
definitionOfDone: Verify-or-block on disk that task-959df79da24442eeb84d446284ff3357 delivered the request/operator capability split, exact state codes/layer, and no live production token-reserve consumer; if absent, report BLOCKED before changing listener routes.

The listener exposes exact-key bounded request and claim bodies under the existing Host/Origin/CSRF/protocol gates; a pending or racing claim refuses exactly `PAIRING_APPROVAL_REQUIRED` at `CONTROL_ROOM_PAIRING_APPROVAL`, and no token-bearing legacy request can mint.

The approval route authenticates before decoding attacker-controlled approval bytes, requires the authenticated principal's project to match the handshake project and `project.admin` capability, and preserves exact authentication/authorization code and layer; confirmation-label possession without that authority grants nothing.

Only the approved matching request invokes the real SessionHandshakePort mint once; mismatched, expired, replayed, concurrent, and foreign requests refuse without minting, and a mint failure cannot accidentally approve or spend another request.

Every response, listener log line, request URL/path, and refusal detail is free of request ids, confirmation labels, operator credentials, pairing bearers, and minted session credentials except the successful claim body returning its credential once to the approved browser.

Focused socket tests cover a legitimate request-approve-claim journey plus a simultaneous attacker request, assert exact code/layer and nonzero hostile roster, and production mutations removing auth/capability or cross-request binding make named assertions red.
taskRails: No legacy bearer/token fallback; unavailable approval state refuses rather than restoring token comparison.
Approval authentication uses the existing production authenticator and project.admin capability; do not create a second operator credential or accept authority in a body field.
Preserve the SessionHandshakePort as the only session mint and keep its project/capability/expiry semantics unchanged.
TDD, exact upstream code/layer preservation, per-production-file size caps, and explicit-pathspec commits apply.

implementationPlan.description: Implement the approval route's authority ordering (DoD 3), which is the security core of this row. In the approve handler, run the EXISTING production HTTP authenticator BEFORE reading or decoding any attacker-controlled approval bytes. Then require, in this order: the authenticated principal's project matches the handshake project, and the principal holds the `project.admin` capability. Surface the authenticator's and authorizer's own code and layer UNCHANGED — do not restamp them into a pairing code, or the layer that actually refused becomes unreadable. Only after all three checks pass may the body be decoded and the confirmation label compared. The label is a correlation value and confers NO authority: possessing a correct label without project.admin must still refuse. Do not create a second operator credential and do not accept authority from any body field (taskRail 2).
implementationPlan.note: Approval ordering is now authenticate (existing authenticateHttpRequest, preserving HttpPortRefused refusal code/layer and local HttpRefused error code/stage) -> pairing availability -> principal project binding -> project.admin -> exact JSON decode -> operator approve. Authorization failures use the existing CAPABILITY_DENIED RuntimeError unchanged with stage AUTHORIZE and HTTP 403; pairing codes are not used to restamp auth refusals. A correct label without admin refuses and the same pending label then succeeds with admin, proving the label confers no authority. Divergence TDD: a foreign-project principal has a Proxy capability roster that throws if `.includes` is consulted; before reorder the focused suite red exactly `capability check ran before project binding`, after reorder exit 0 with Test Files 1 passed / Tests 8 passed.

implementationPlan.description: DIVERGENCE ARMS for the two guards this row adds, in a new `apps/daemon/src/http/http-listener-pairing-routes.test.ts`. Each guard needs a fixture where it is the ONLY mechanism that can refuse. (A) AUTH-BEFORE-DECODE: send a MALFORMED approval body from an UNAUTHENTICATED caller and assert the AUTHENTICATOR's code and layer answer — not a decode/PAIRING_CONFIRMATION_INVALID refusal. Pair it with the same malformed body from an AUTHENTICATED project.admin principal, which must now reach the decoder and refuse with the decode code. The two inputs differ only in credentials, so the pair proves ORDERING rather than merely that both refuse. (B) CAPABILITY: an authenticated principal in the correct project WITHOUT project.admin, presenting a CORRECT confirmation label, must refuse with the capability code — proving the label confers nothing. Pair with the same principal holding project.admin, which succeeds. Build the hostile cases from an immutable frozen roster with an EXACT nonzero length assertion and member uniqueness so an emptied sweep cannot pass; assert exact code AND layer on every case.
implementationPlan.note: Divergence arms are production-surface pure-handler calls. AUTH-BEFORE-DECODE now reuses the exact same frozen malformed bytes (valid JSON with an extra injectedAuthority key) for unauthenticated and authenticated project.admin calls: only credential differs; answers are AUTHENTICATION_FAILED/stage AUTHENTICATE/401 versus PAIRING_CONFIRMATION_INVALID/layer CONTROL_ROOM_PAIRING_APPROVAL/400. CAPABILITY uses one live correct label: same principal id/project without admin gets CAPABILITY_DENIED/stage AUTHORIZE/403, then with admin gets APPROVED. Foreign-project admin also gets CAPABILITY_DENIED/AUTHORIZE, and a proxy roster proves project binding runs before capability access. HOSTILE_APPROVAL_CASES is frozen, exact length 5, >0, and unique. Custom authenticator port refusal pins its exact code OPERATOR_SESSION_REVOKED and layer SESSION_AUTHORITY unchanged. Fresh focused exit 0: Test Files 1 passed / Tests 8 passed.

4. UNCHANGED AND STILL THE CORE OF THE ROW: the authenticated approve route does not exist, and DoD 3's authenticate-BEFORE-decode ordering, the `project.admin` capability requirement, and the "confirmation label confers nothing" property are all genuinely unbuilt.
```
expected { ok: true, state: 'APPROVED' } to deeply equal { code: "LISTENER_ROUTE_UNKNOWN", … }
```
The daemon answered `{ ok: true, state: "APPROVED" }` to the agent's own credential.
